notes: EBIT is not directly disclosed as a single GAAP line; this package calculates EBIT as (Income before income taxes from continuing operations + interest expense). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000027/ibmars2025.pdf))

D&A equals depreciation plus amortization of capitalized software and acquired intangible assets from the consolidated cash flow statement. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000027/ibmars2025.pdf))

Capex is approximated as cash payments for property, plant and equipment plus investment in software (both from investing cash flows); disposals and other investing cash flow movements are not modeled separately. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000027/ibmars2025.pdf))

Historical NWC equals IBM-reported working capital (current assets minus current liabilities) and may include cash and short-term debt effects; forecast NWC is modeled as a percent of sales rather than explicitly projecting each working capital line item. ([ibm.com](https://www.ibm.com/downloads/documents/us-en/1227c12d3a38b173))

WACC and terminal exit multiple are modeling assumptions (not directly extracted from filings); run sensitivity in the DCF. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

NOL balance could not be reliably extracted as a discrete cash-tax NOL amount within the time budget of this pipeline; nol_balance is set to null and utilization is assumed at 0.80. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000027/ibmars2025.pdf))

Comps EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA may not be explicitly NTM in all sources; StockAnalysis often provides EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA plus forward P/E, so EV multiples are treated as valuation proxies.

catalysts: Sustained software and infrastructure growth (hybrid cloud/AI demand) translating into durable operating leverage. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))
Free cash flow conversion improvements enabling additional shareholder returns (dividends and buybacks). ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))
Execution on large delivery cycles (consulting backlog realization and infrastructure deployments) moving results toward bull-case growth/margin.
company_overview: IBM is a software-led enterprise platform with integrated offerings across Software, Consulting, and Infrastructure.
The strategy emphasizes hybrid cloud and AI, supported by enterprise software (including Red Hat) and consulting delivery at scale.
IBM also runs an in-house financing segment that supports client transactions and is reflected within consolidated results.
current_context: FY2025 revenue was $67.5B and free cash flow was $14.7B, with management highlighting revenue/profit durability into 2026. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

FY2026 expectations: more than 5% constant-currency revenue growth and free cash flow up by about $1B year-over-year. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))
In Q4 2025, IBM reported a generative AI book of business of more than $12.5B. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

Balance sheet flexibility: cash, restricted cash, and marketable securities were about $14.5B and total debt about $61.3B at year-end 2025. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes revenue growth moderates from FY2026 guidance toward low-to-mid single digits by FY2030, consistent with a mature IT services/software mix. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

EBIT margin is modeled to stabilize near high-17% levels versus the volatility in GAAP tax/interest items, reflecting ongoing mix and productivity initiatives. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000027/ibmars2025.pdf))

Capital intensity is kept steady (capex ~2.5–2.7% of sales; D&A ~7.4–7.5% of sales), aligning with historical depreciation/amortization and cash flow investing lines. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000027/ibmars2025.pdf))

Working capital is modeled near flat-to-slightly negative as a conservative cash conversion profile for an integrated platform business. ([ibm.com](https://www.ibm.com/downloads/documents/us-en/1227c12d3a38b173))

Terminal value uses an exit multiple approach with a mature IT-services valuation range, cross-checked against peer EV/EBITDA and forward P/E snapshots. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/bcba/INFY/statistics/))
key_risks: Enterprise IT budget delays or slowdown leading to revenue growth below the modeled path. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

Margin compression from wage/cost inflation, mix shifts, or weaker pricing power versus base-case EBIT margin stabilization. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000027/ibmars2025.pdf))
Tax and pension effects creating volatility versus a DCF that assumes a stable normalized tax rate.
